result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers catch the contradiction, tie each vague remark to the leave-request form, rota view and expenses screen, and ask for dated fixes in the contract with a remedy or exit. B does better on evidence: it puts product version, test date, self-assessment versus independent audit, method, and screen reader and browser combinations at the front of its questions. A leaves out the product version and who did the testing. B is also slightly tighter and better ordered, while A adds WCAG detail the request didn't need. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers catch the contradiction, link each vague remark to the leave-request form, rota view and expenses screen, and ask for dated fixes with a contractual remedy or exit. A asks for the evidence first: product version, date, conformance level, whether it was self-assessed or audited, the test method and the assistive tech used. It is also slightly tighter and better ordered. B adds useful detail, such as WCAG criterion numbers, a list-view alternative for the rota and drag-and-drop examples, but it is longer, never asks which product version was tested, and leaves the testing-method questions until late.
